brief.headline: July closed with the tightness signature fully intact - the 30-Jul official (still the latest published) has cash at $3,231.00, the backwardation at +$44.00 and stock at a century low of 266,300 t - and the LME's day-delayed close shows Friday's 31-Jul session HELD the ground (3M closing $3,195.50, +0.49%) despite China's first factory contraction since February.
bullets: WHERE THE MONTH ENDED: Friday's 31-Jul official prints on the public source (Westmetall) on Monday, but two independent public reads say the complex closed the month firm - the LME's own day-delayed 3-month CLOSING price for 31-Jul was $3,195.50 (+0.49%) and Trading Economics' traded reference finished $3,194.00 (+0.48%), taking July to +3.14% month-on-month. The tightness evidence built through the final week - backwardation widening +$16.00 to +$30.00 to +$44.00 and a 22-session unbroken stock draw - survived first contact with the sub-50 China PMI.

THE MONTH IN ONE NUMBER: the July-2026 monthly mean settled at $3,150.50 cash / $3,145.69 3M (Westmetall averages), 8.9% BELOW June's $3,458.64 - July was the month the June war-premium spike deflated and then stabilised. The month's low ($3,061.50 on 02-Jul) and the month's high ($3,231.00 on 30-Jul) bracket a market that spent four weeks rebuilding from the post-truce washout, and finished at the top of the range.

DEMAND VERSUS SUPPLY IS NOW THE WHOLE DEBATE: China's July PMIs (manufacturing 49.2, non-manufacturing 49.0, composite 49.3) are the clearest public demand warning since February, and July alumina/raw-material weakness cuts the cost floor. Against that, the supply side hardened further - analysts covering the Gulf now pencil in 3-3.5 Mt of regional output losses through 2026, roughly 5% of global primary supply, with Gulf war-risk insurance quoted at 3-10% of hull value (over $7m per transit on a $100m vessel).

WHAT TO WATCH NEXT: Monday brings the Caixin manufacturing PMI (the private-sector cross-check on the official 49.2) AND Westmetall's publication of the 31-Jul official - the first official struck after the PMI - which confirms whether the +$44.00 backwardation held. Then the run rate on LME stock (breaks 265,000 t within days at the July draw pace), Hormuz transit counts after the first LNG exit in three weeks, and Q4 MJP talks opening late August against Century Aluminum results on 06-Aug and Alba's H1 due early August.

STILL THE LATEST PUBLISHED OFFICIAL at this Saturday 01-Aug compile (~06:00 London): Westmetall posts Friday's official the next business day, so the 31-Jul print lands Monday - no figure on this board reflects Friday's session or carries the Chinese PMI in an official price yet. avg = JULY-2026 monthly mean $3,150.50 as published on Westmetall's averages page (the month has rolled; June was $3,458.64). Disclosure: the arithmetic mean of the 22 daily officials published 01-30 Jul computes to $3,154.16 - the small difference reflects the source's own inclusion convention; the published figure is carried.

Support $3,159.50 then $3,133 / $3,116; resistance $3,303 then $3,392.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: BACKWARDATION (cash ABOVE 3M) at +$44.00 on the 30-Jul official, up from +$30.00 on 29-Jul and +$16.00 on 28-Jul - a third consecutive session of widening and the widest prompt premium of the move. Convention: cash > 3M = backwardation = nearby tightness. The spread has widened through three different flat-price regimes (down $32.50, up $47.50, up $24.00), which points at physical availability rather than directional speculation, corroborated by exchange stock at a century low of 266,300 t. The +$44.00 is the widest month-end prompt premium of 2026. The first hard test - the spread on the officials struck after China's 49.2 PMI - is published Monday.

lme.commentary: SATURDAY COMPILE, MONTH-END EDITION: every official on this board is the 30-JULY-2026 print - re-verified live on Westmetall this morning - because the source publishes Friday's official the next business day; the 31-Jul official lands Monday. What CAN be said about Friday publicly: the LME's own day-delayed 3M CLOSING price for 31-Jul was $3,195.50 (+0.49%) and Trading Economics' traded reference closed $3,194.00 (+0.48%), July +3.12% m/m - the session HELD the week's gains into the monthly close despite China's 49.2 PMI landing that morning, which is itself informative: the first market test of the tightness structure against a contractionary demand print did not crack it. July's monthly means are now locked: cash $3,150.50, 3M $3,145.69, average stock 283,969 t (all Westmetall) - respectively -8.9%, -8.5% and -11.3% versus June, the month the war-premium spike deflated into a floor. The final week's structure was the story: backwardation +$16.00 to +$30.00 to +$44.00 through three different price regimes, stock drawing every single session (22 straight) to 266,300 t, and the whole base-metals board on one uniform 30-Jul session - copper 13,770 (+1.19%), zinc 3,601 (+0.61%), nickel 17,170 (-0.15%), lead 1,900 (-0.73%) on 3M.

regional.basis: Q3-2026 SETTLED at $395/t CIF Japan (S&P Global Platts, assessed 06-Jul-2026) - an 11-year high (prior peak Q3-2014 $404/t), +11.9-12.9% q/q vs Q2's $350-353, built from 10 trades at $395/t for a combined minimum 15,500 t/month, July-September loading. QUARTERLY BASIS: this does not re-price daily and no fresher public print exists at this 01-Aug refresh. Q4-2026 talks are expected to open around late August - into an LME backwardation of +$44.00, a century-low exchange stock, an 11-year-high starting point, but also a Chinese manufacturing PMI in contraction at 49.2 and a yen back below 160 that raises Japanese buyers' local-currency cost. AL Circle's 24-Jul review notes the CIF Japan premium rose 127% quarter-on-quarter in early 2026 - context for why buyers resisted producer offers of $440-480. avg = Q1-26 settlement ($195).

Platts CIF Japan spot P1020/P1020A $370/t over LME cash, assessed 06-Jul-2026. PERIODIC ASSESSMENT - the freshest publicly retrievable mark, now 26 days old at this 01-Aug refresh; it is carried at its assessment date and is NOT a current-session value. No daily move should be inferred. Against the 30-Jul cash official of $3,231.00 an all-in Japanese delivered equivalent computes to roughly $3,601/t, of which the premium is about 10.3%. USD/JPY back below 160 (159.96 at the 30-Jul read, -2.1%) raises the local-currency cost of dollar metal at the margin as Q4 negotiations approach.

European P1020A duty-unpaid in-warehouse Rotterdam, carried at its last public assessment. PERIODIC ASSESSMENT, not a daily mark - no fresher free public print is available at this 01-Aug refresh, so the value is held at its assessment date rather than implied to have moved. The duty-unpaid leg is the cleanest read on genuine European physical tightness because it excludes both the 6% EU import duty and the CBAM cost embedded in duty-paid assessments since January 2026.

6063 extrusion billet premium, in-warehouse duty-paid Rotterdam (Fastmarkets MB-AL-0002 basis), carried at its last public assessment date. PERIODIC ASSESSMENT - not refreshed daily. Billet premiums carry the duty-paid structure plus the conversion spread over P1020, so they move with both metal availability and extruder order books; European extrusion demand remains the soft spot in the regional balance, and TTF gas around EUR 58.5/MWh (30-Jul read, -3.4% on the session but +32% on the month) still caps restart economics. EGA's force majeure on European billet contracts, declared 12-Apr-2026, was still in force at the last public check (20-Jul).

US Midwest transaction premium, carried at its last public assessment date. PERIODIC ASSESSMENT, not a daily mark. TARIFF-INFLATED: not comparable with pre-2026 history because Section 232 at 50% sits inside it. Public context from AL Circle's 24-Jul supply-chain review: the Midwest premium broke $2,000/t for the first time in January 2026 and has since traded above $2,400/t, putting the all-in delivered cost to a US manufacturer regularly above $5,500/t even when the LME itself is calm. See the decomposition on the US duty-paid row.

US Midwest duty-paid P1020A premium, carried at its last public assessment date (periodic, not daily). THE TARIFF DECOMPOSITION IS RE-COMPUTED EVERY RUN because it is a function of the current LME cash official: at the 30-Jul cash of $3,231.00 (still the latest published official at this 01-Aug refresh) the Section 232 leg alone is 0.50 x $3,231.00 = $1,615.50/t. Every $100 on LME cash mechanically adds $50/t of tariff cost to US duty-paid metal before any change in physical tightness. The residual over the tariff leg is the genuine market premium; the dashboard computes it from the current cash rather than fabricating a freight/financing/tightness split. The 50% articles / 25% derivative structure was re-verified against the June-2026 proclamation (Federal Register 2026-11314) at this refresh - no change.

tariffs.note: Structural floor plus carbon border adjustment

drivers.text: Geopolitical risk has become a standing input cost: Gulf war-risk cover is 3-10% of hull value - over $7 million per transit on a $100m vessel - versus 0.25% pre-war — AL Circle's 24-Jul Middle East review assembles the public picture: war-risk insurance for Gulf transits stood at roughly 0.25% of hull value before February's escalation, quadrupled within three weeks of the first strikes, and by mid-July was quoted at 3-10% - the difference between a $250,000 premium and one exceeding $7 million on a single transit. Around 90% of ocean-going tonnage covered by the International Group of P&I Clubs faces cancellation-and-repricing clauses on short notice. Lloyd's underwriters say cover remains technically available, but traceable large-vessel crossings on the main safe-transit corridor ground close to a halt in July. The five GCC smelters produced about 6.16 Mt in 2025 (roughly 8% of world supply) with more than 80% exported; analysts now pencil in 3-3.5 Mt of losses through 2026, near 5% of global primary supply. The direction turned two-way in the final week of July - a QatarEnergy-controlled LNG tanker exited Hormuz on 30-Jul, the first in nearly three weeks - so this driver is no longer one-way support, but the insurance wedge unwinds far more slowly than a single transit.
drivers.source: AL Circle - 2026 Middle East aluminium outlook: 5% of global supply, USD 7 million insurance and the Hormuz effect (24-Jul-2026)

drivers.text: US Section 232 at 50% is $1,615.50/t of the US duty-paid premium at the 30-Jul cash - the rate was re-verified unchanged this run — Aluminium articles made entirely or almost entirely of aluminium pay 50% ad valorem on full customs value; derivative aluminium content pays 25%. The structure originates in the April-2026 proclamation and was further adjusted by the 01-Jun-2026 proclamation (Federal Register 2026-11314, effective 08-Jun-2026), whose 08-Jun-2026 to 31-Dec-2027 window applies to the Annex I-C reduced-rate carve-outs - 15% all-in for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and EU members. A 20-Jul-2026 proclamation additionally lets companies with an approved plan to build or expand a US primary smelter (construction beginning by 20-Jan-2029) import at half the applicable rate; no CBP guidance for that measure has been issued yet. MECHANICS: at the 30-Jul cash official of $3,231.00 the tariff leg is 0.50 x 3,231.00 = $1,615.50/t. The policy leg moves with the metal price whether or not the physical market changes at all.
drivers.source: Federal Register 2026-11314 - Further adjusting the tariff regimes for imports of aluminum, steel and copper (June 2026); CBP Section 232 guidance

drivers.text: The EU stack is duty plus CBAM: 6% import duty, and since January 2026 the benchmark Rotterdam duty-paid assessment embeds CBAM cost — The EU applies a 6% import duty on primary aluminium from non-preferential origins. Separately, from January 2026 Fastmarkets' benchmark European P1020A in-warehouse duty-paid Rotterdam assessment includes CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) costs in the same way it already reflects the import duty. That methodology change has a real consequence: the European duty-paid premium is no longer a pure physical-tightness signal - it is a physical signal plus two policy layers, which is why the duty-UNPAID assessment is carried alongside it as the cleaner read on genuine regional availability. The 31-Jul Eurostat flash estimate adds a macro edge: euro-area energy inflation jumped to 10.0% in July from 8.5%, the Middle East passthrough that keeps European smelting the marginal-cost capacity and the region import-dependent.
drivers.source: Fastmarkets - Aluminium P1020A premium, in-whs dp Rotterdam methodology (CBAM inclusion from January 2026)

drivers.text: The demand-side counterweight is now on the table: China's July PMI at 49.2 was the first factory contraction since February, and premiums are ultimately a demand-pull signal — Official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.2 in July from 50.3 in June against consensus of 50.1 - the first sub-50 reading since February 2026 - with non-manufacturing at 49.0 (from 50.2) and the composite output index at 49.3. China is roughly 60% of world primary output and the single largest block of demand. Regional premiums are a function of where metal wants to go: a contracting Chinese factory sector both frees up domestic units and weakens the pull that supports ex-China premiums. SMM's end-July spot commentary corroborates soft physical tone inside China - central-China ingot transactions at discounts of RMB 100-140/t to the SHFE August contract with weak downstream procurement, even as consumption-region ingot inventory still destocked modestly. The print post-dates every official price on this board; the first officials struck after it publish Monday.
drivers.source: Xinhua / China NBS - China's July PMIs (31-Jul-2026); SMM spot aluminium midday review via AL Circle (29-Jul-2026)

notes: Alumina is the largest single raw-material line in the smelter cost stack, so the direction of travel matters as much as the level. At roughly $328-330/t FOB Australia against a $3,187 3M official, alumina is about 10.3% of the metal price - historically low - and every public China indicator (7.028 Mt national inventory and building, RMB 100-140/t discounts to the SHFE August contract, a 75% operating rate on 88.86 Mt/y of capacity) points the same way: the cost floor under aluminium is FALLING while the metal price holds. That is margin expansion for smelters, and it is one reason peer earnings surprised to the upside across July's reporting.

The ex-China balance is a surplus with a shrinking edge: S&P CERA models +1.79 Mt globally for 2026 (from +2.4 Mt in 2025), EGA's Al Taweelah is ramping back toward full capability by year-end (it met 46% of EGA's feedstock needs pre-outage), and against that Rio Tinto's Yarwun cut removes roughly 1.2 Mt/y - about 40% of the refinery - from October 2026. The CME FOB Australia futures curve at $309.40 (24-Jul settlement) prices the surplus persisting.

Raw-material inputs BELOW alumina are also soft or stable: Guinea bauxite around $70/dmt with record H1 shipments of 114.8 Mt (+15% y/y), caustic flat month-on-month in the July contract cycle at Shanxi plants, lime steady. Nothing in the refining cost stack currently argues for alumina price support beyond freight and the Yarwun adjustment.

Marks on this table are periodic assessments carried at their published dates - the FOB Western Australia spot is 23 days old, the Platts print 36 days, the SMM index 16 days, the CME settlement 8 days. Where SMM's daily commentary describes direction since the last dated level (correction, fluctuating trend, inventory buildup), that direction is reported without inventing a number.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: The picture stayed two-way into month-end. After Tehran rejected Oman's proposed 50-50 transit arrangement on 29-Jul and crude surged nearly 7%, a QatarEnergy-controlled LNG tanker exited the strait bound for Pakistan on 30-Jul - the first in nearly three weeks - and oil eased as tankers continued to ply conflict-zone waters; Brent still closed July more than 20% higher on the month. The structural numbers are unchanged and public: roughly 9% of global primary aluminium capacity sits behind this waterway, more than 80% of Gulf metal is exported, Gulf output was -34.5% y/y in June, and analysts covering the region pencil in 3-3.5 Mt of industry-wide losses through 2026 - near 5% of global primary supply (AL Circle, 24-Jul). Traceable large-vessel crossings on the main safe-transit corridor ground close to a halt in July per Lloyd's underwriters. Whether the late-July departures become a trend is the single largest swing factor in the premium structure into August.

logistics.label: Red Sea corridor
logistics.note: Bab el-Mandeb traffic has been reported steady despite the Houthi threat, keeping the Suez routing viable for Europe-bound metal and alumina. This remains the less binding of the two chokepoints, but it is a second-order exposure that would compound sharply if Hormuz stays shut into Q4.

logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance
logistics.note: War-risk premiums for Gulf transits are quoted at 3-10% of hull value against roughly 0.25% before the conflict - a $250,000 premium becoming one exceeding $7 million per transit on a $100 million vessel (AL Circle / Reuters / The National reporting compiled 24-Jul). Cover quadrupled within three weeks of the first strikes and climbed toward 3% by early July before the current 3-10% range. Around 90% of ocean-going tonnage covered by the International Group of P&I Clubs faces cancellation-and-repricing clauses on short notice, so the effective cost of a contested-strait transit rises before any cargo is damaged. This remains the single largest non-tariff cost wedge in Gulf-origin delivered prices.

logistics.label: Baltic Dry Index (BDI)
logistics.note: The Baltic Dry Index closed the month at 2,732 on Friday 31-Jul, up 59 points on the day and rebounding from 2,671 - though still below the mid-July peak near 2,944 (Baltic Exchange via Hellenic Shipping News). Dry-bulk direction matters most for bauxite and alumina freight into China, where Guinea shipped a record 114.8 Mt in H1. A firming BDI at the margin re-widens the freight leg of the alumina surplus math.

logistics.label: Container freight (Drewry WCI)
logistics.note: Drewry's World Container Index fell 4% to $4,374 per 40ft on 23-Jul (last published weekly print at this refresh), with Shanghai-Rotterdam at $4,824, after peaking at $4,639 on 09-Jul - the highest since September 2024 and roughly 61% above a year earlier. Direction is easing, but several carriers have filed Emergency Fuel Surcharges effective August 2026 on continued Hormuz disruption, so realised container cost falls more slowly than the index and the August invoices carry the new surcharges from this week.

catalysts.text: WESTMETALL PUBLISHES THE 31-JUL OFFICIAL (and Monday's 03-Aug official follows) - the first officials struck after China's sub-50 PMI. The single most informative tell available: whether the cash-3M backwardation held above roughly +$40.00 into a contractionary demand print. Holding would strongly confirm the tightness is physical; a rapid collapse toward flat would say the spread was carrying macro and speculative content

China Caixin manufacturing PMI for July - the private-survey cross-check on the official 49.2. Caixin skews toward smaller, export-oriented coastal manufacturers, so divergence between the two locates the weakness (state vs private sector) rather than confirming it economy-wide

Whether LME stock breaks 265,000 t - the draw has run 22 consecutive published sessions at roughly -1,600 t/day, which breaks the level within days on the July run rate. The more important variable is the AVAILABLE on-warrant component, at a 16-month low and dominated by Russian-origin material

Hormuz transit counts - after the first LNG exit in nearly three weeks (30-Jul), whether normalisation sustains or reverses. Roughly 9% of global primary capacity sits behind the waterway; 3-3.5 Mt of 2026 losses (~5% of global supply) is the current public estimate; war-risk cover at 3-10% of hull value is the slow-moving wedge

Alba H1-2026 results expected - the direct Gulf-disruption read after a Q1 that printed +316% y/y ($200.3m) BEFORE the March strikes' full effect; the H1 print shows what force majeure at roughly a fifth of capacity does to the P&L; Maaden (1211) Q2-2026 results are likewise expected in early August on prior-year cadence (Q2-2025 was reported in the first week of August 2025 via SPA/Tadawul) - together the two direct Gulf/Saudi listed-producer reads on the disruption quarter
Century Aluminum Q2-2026 results - the purest US/Section-232 read in the sector, with Mt. Holly back at full capacity from 27-Jul and the Midwest premium above $2,400/t all quarter

SMM weekly China aluminium ingot and billet social inventory - the direct test of whether a contracting PMI is translating into physical destocking or restocking. Billet inventory had built for two consecutive weeks to 121,000 t as at 23-Jul, an off-season demand signal that pre-dated the PMI; end-July spot reviews still showed modest consumption-region destocking (Guangdong, Wuxi)

Q4-2026 MJP CIF Japan premium negotiations expected to open - Q3 settled at $395/t, an 11-year high. Talks open against a widening LME backwardation and century-low stock, but also a contracting Chinese PMI, a firmer yen (below 160) and a premium that has already risen 127% q/q earlier in the year

China August PMIs and industrial output - whether July's 49.2 was a single-month distortion or the start of a demand downturn. Two consecutive contractionary prints would materially change the balance estimates underpinning the 720-930 kt deficit consensus

FOMC with a Summary of Economic Projections - the July meeting held 9-3 with three dissents FOR a hike, the most opposite-direction dissents since September 2016; June core PCE at 3.3% argues patience. The SEP shows whether the hawkish minority is spreading to the median dot

Indonesian and Chinese capacity additions landing against consensus expectations of 2027-28 surpluses - the structural counterweight to the current squeeze. Indonesia ~705 kt in 2026 with Tsingshan's further 800 kt at Weda Bay planned for 2027-28

risks.text: CHINA DEMAND HAS TURNED - July manufacturing PMI 49.2, the first contraction since February 2026, with non-manufacturing 49.0 and composite 49.3; SMM end-July physical commentary shows central-China discounts of RMB 100-140/t and weak downstream procurement. If Monday's Caixin print and the August SMM inventory series confirm it, the 720-930 kt deficit consensus starts eroding from the demand side

Tightening risk is DEFERRED, NOT REMOVED - the Fed held 9-3 and the Bank of England 6-3, each with three dissents FOR a hike; the cooler June core PCE (3.3%) leans against the hawks but the euro area's energy-led re-acceleration (July flash 2.9%, energy 10.0%) leans with them. September's FOMC dot plot is the decision point for the dollar leg of the metals trade

Hormuz normalisation would erode the premium floor - the first LNG transit in nearly three weeks exited 30-Jul and oil eased into month-end; if transits normalise durably, the largest single component of the premium structure (war-risk at 3-10% of hull value, over $7m per transit) begins to unwind, though insurance reprices far more slowly than transit counts

Indonesian and Chinese supply overwhelms the deficit - Indonesia adds ~705 kt in 2026 (+89% y/y) with Tsingshan planning 800 kt more at Weda Bay; China is operating THROUGH its 45 Mt cap at 45.31 Mt/y; Century Mt. Holly is back at full rate; consensus already expects 2027 surpluses. The 2026 squeeze and the 2027-28 wave are the same trade in two acts

The backwardation is thin-market rather than consumption driven - a prompt premium set by a 266,300 t stock base and a 16-month-low on-warrant pool (dominated by Russian-origin metal) can collapse on modest re-warranting without any demand change; month-end index rebalancing and option expiry can distort the prompt independently of physical conditions

Falling alumina and raw materials remove cost-push support - China alumina inventory 7.028 Mt and building, the SMM index drifting lower with the medium-term downtrend intact, bauxite ~$70/dmt on record Guinea shipments; a falling cost floor supports margins today but lowers the level producers defend if demand keeps weakening

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. China alone ran a 322 kt deficit in June, and exchange inventory at a fresh century low leaves no absorption capacity

Consensus expects surpluses as Gulf output recovers and Indonesia ramps; Concord Resources warns the market may be 'too complacent about supply risks' in the meantime. Rio Tinto's 40% Yarwun alumina cut from October 2026 trims one input to that surplus
